transcript:
Meeting: Meadowline Systems x Redwood Inference — API fitment & hosting pathway
Date/Time: 2026-10-19 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jia (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM); Carlos (Meadowline Head of ML), Rina (CTO), Ethan (Infra)

Auto-generated summary:
- Meadowline is evaluating Redwood's hosted API for a fast prototype but is considering Dedicated/Private for PII-sensitive workflows and predictable latency.
- Primary concerns: latency at 75-150ms token for short-form responses, cost per 1M tokens at scale, VPC/KMS for data at rest and audit logs.
- Agreed next steps: share quickstart code, Dedicated SKU sheet, and a prompt set for a short pilot.

Topics:
- Quickstart & free credits (time-to-first-token)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2/KMS/VPC and audit logs
- Performance: latency targets, batching, KV cache behaviors
- Pilot design & success criteria

Action items (auto):
- Send pricing + SKUs
- Share quickstart repo and notebook
- Customer to share prompt templates and stakeholders

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): All right, hey everyone, thanks for making the time. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this account. Jia's the SE, she'll jump into perf stuff. Maya's here to help with onboarding. How are you all doing?
[00:12] Carlos: Hey, good, thanks. Rina and Ethan are with me. We wanted to get a sense for fastest path to try Redwood for some search summarization and internal agent helpers.
[00:22] Rina: Yeah, main ask is — we want to prototype quickly with hosted, see time-to-first-token, but we have some production requirements that may push us to Dedicated or private VPC later.
[00:34] Jia (Redwood): Totally makes sense. Quick question up front: do you have any hard requirements around data residency or air-gapped?
[00:40] Carlos: Not air-gapped right now. But some of our logs contain customer identifiers; we need KMS encryption at rest and audit logs. We're SOC 2 in progress.
[00:49] Samir: That's pretty common. We have hosted with SOC2 and audit logs available; for extra isolation we can propose Redwood Dedicated or VPC private deployment. Both support KMS and customer-managed keys for Private.
[00:59] Ethan: How different is the integration effort? Our infra team wants to know how much work to switch from hosted pilot to Dedicated.
[01:07] Samir: Good question. The API surface is the same — hosted, dedicated, private all use the same REST/SDK. Biggest work is networking for private — VPC peering or private link and some IAM roles for on-prem. Dedicated is basically reserved capacity you call the same endpoints but with a different region/pool, so switching is mainly config and a little rollout work.
[01:30] Rina: What's the typical lead time for Dedicated? We don't want a multi-month procurement to block.
[01:36] Jia: For reserved pools we typically have a 2–6 week provisioning depending on GPU availability; for pilot-sized pools we can often fast-track. If you want a short pilot with predictable latency we can carve a small Dedicated pool for a few weeks as part of a paid pilot.
[01:52] Carlos: Okay — cost is a big factor. For a POC we prefer starting hosted with the free credits if you have them. Do you still offer credits for quickstarts?
[01:59] Samir: Yes, we have PLG credits for new signups and we also allocate partner credits for pilots. We'll outline the credits and the path to first token — typically teams can go from signup to first request in under an hour if they use the SDK and our sample prompts.
[02:14] Carlos: Under an hour is key. Our devs like to run a quick curl or python example and confirm responses.
[02:19] Jia: We'll share a minimal quickstart repo — curl, python, and a simple node example. Also a pre-built prompt-set that mimics your summarization flow so you can run against it and compare.
[02:29] Ethan: For latency, our target is — when the model returns short summaries it should be under 300ms 95th for interactive use, and ideally under 150ms. Are those realistic?
[02:39] Jia: Depends on model and sequence length. For short summaries with ~40 tokens, the hosted low-latency configs hit around 100–200ms p95 on our smaller open models; for stricter 150ms p95 you'd probably want Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching turned off for single-shot requests. Also prefix K V cache can help if you're re-asking similar contexts but that's more relevant for chat/agent flows.
[03:01] Rina: K V cache? Did you mean KV cache?
[03:03] Jia: Yes, sorry — KV cache. There's an auto prefix cache that helps for repeated contexts. Sometimes the transcribe here says K V cash — ignore that, sorry.
[03:15] Carlos: We're also curious about function/tool calling and structured output — we need JSON responses to map fields into our downstream services.
[03:22] Samir: The API supports structured outputs and simple function calling primitives. We also have validators and response schemas in the SDK to reduce post-processing mismatches.
[03:31] Ethan: On the security front, can you integrate with our KMS? We use a cloud provider-managed KMS but want to hold keys ourselves.
[03:39] Jia: For Private deployments you can bring keys (HSM/KMS integration). For Hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS in some regions — I'll confirm the exact cloud provider requirements in the doc I send.
[03:52] Rina: And audit logs? We need change logs for model versions and who called what.
[03:58] Maya (Redwood): We can export audit logs to your SIEM (S3, BigQuery, or Splunk); logs include token-level metadata, model versions, route used, and the user ID if you pass it through the request. We'll include an architecture note.
[04:13] Carlos: Great. On evaluation metrics — we'd like to run a quick quality check: response relevancy, hallucination rate, latency and cost per 1M tokens. Thoughts on a small benchmark?
[04:24] Jia: We recommend a 2-week pilot with 2 prompt sets: one for summarization templates and one for agent-style Q&A. We'll run both hosted and a small Dedicated pool to compare latency and cost. We'll provide an eval harness and a sample spreadsheet to track hallucination and token counts.
[04:40] Carlos: Sounds good. Any gotchas moving from hosted to private with the same prompt set?
[04:46] Jia: The model binaries may be a slightly different quantization profile on Dedicated/Private depending on GPU; you'll rarely see quality regressions but it's why we do model-variant A/B tests. We'll surface any delta.
[04:58] Rina: How about rate limits? We expect bursts from our web clients — can you do autoscaling?
[05:04] Samir: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity; hosted has per-account quotas that we can raise for pilots. We'll give recommended traffic shaping patterns and client-side backoff guidance.
[05:16] Ethan: For the pilot, what's the minimum commit or spend?
[05:20] Samir: For a Dedicated pilot we usually ask for a 1–3 month pilot with a small reserved commit, but we also do short-term burst capacity trials. We'll include options: purely hosted pilot with credits, hosted plus short Dedicated carve-out for a few weeks, or Private eval (longer lead time).
[05:37] Carlos: Is there any prebuilt connector for our vector DB? We use an in-house embeddings store but may test hybrid reranking.
[05:44] Jia: We don't require a specific vector store; we can provide embedding APIs and a sample connector for common stores. For reranking it's a simple flow: generate embeddings, run an ANN search, then call the model for re-ranking. We'll share a snippet.
[05:58] Rina: One nit — we have procurement constraints and need line-item cost for budgeting. Can you send expected cost per 1M tokens for both hosted and Dedicated?
[06:07] Samir: Yes — I'll send a breakdown. Hosted is usage-based per token; Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing and lower unit economics at higher throughput. We'll include a sample TCO sheet for your expected traffic.
[06:21] Carlos: Perfect. Also, on SSO and RBAC — we use SAML for internal tools.
[06:26] Maya: We support SAML SSO and granular RBAC for team provisioning. We'll attach the SSO setup guide.
[06:34] Ethan: Quick technical question: how do you handle long-running agent sessions and KV cache eviction? We worry about memory growth.
[06:42] Jia: The runtime manages KV caches with LRU eviction and fixed-size shard buckets; for long-lived sessions we recommend session windowing or external caching for very long histories. We can show the config knobs.
[06:58] Carlos: Ok that's helpful. If we start with hosted, how do we measure the migration cost to Dedicated? Is there a migration checklist?
[07:06] Samir: Yes — we have a migration playbook: network prep (VPC/peering), service account and IAM mapping, model pinning and rollout policy, smoke tests and blue/green traffic shift. Jia will send a condensed checklist.
[07:20] Rina: As for success criteria — for us pilot success is: 1) integration within two weeks, 2) summaries reach >85% precision in our eval set, 3) latency below 200ms p95 for interactive routes.
[07:31] Samir: Noted. Those are reasonable. We'll tailor the pilot to capture those metrics.
[07:36] Carlos: One more: do you support on-prem packaging if we get to regulated workloads?
[07:41] Jia: Yes — the Private deployment includes an on-prem option; it's higher friction/time but supports air-gapped setups. We'll include the high-level timeline.
[07:51] Rina: Great. Can you also include a simple SLA for Dedicated? We need to compare to other vendors.
[07:56] Samir: We'll attach the standard SLA for Dedicated pools — uptime targets and latency SLOs.
[08:02] Ethan: For instrumentation, does the Console expose per-request token cost?
[08:07] Maya: Yes — the Console gives token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and traces. You can also instrument custom metrics via our tracing hooks.
[08:16] Carlos: Okay, let's talk next steps. We'll start with hosted trial using credits, run the quickstart with the sample prompts, then decide if we need a small Dedicated carve-out.
[08:25] Samir: Perfect. I'll send the quickstart repo, pricing SKUs, and a pilot proposal. Jia will put together a perf checklist and the migration playbook. Maya will add the SSO and security docs.
[08:37] Rina: Who will be the point of contact?
[08:39] Carlos: For us, I'll coordinate and Rina will own security, Ethan will lead infra.
[08:45] Samir: Great — Carlos, Rina, Ethan noted. We'll follow up with that bundle by Friday.
[08:51] Carlos: Sweet. One quick clarification — do you have examples for function calling to output strict JSON schemas?
[08:56] Jia: Yes; the sample repo includes a validator that enforces schema on response and will rerun generation up to N times. We'll share that.
[09:05] Ethan: Awesome. Any final Qs from Redwood side?
[09:09] Maya: No — just to confirm I have the right contacts for procurement.
[09:12] Rina: Send them to me, I'll route internally.
[09:15] Samir: All right, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the documents and schedule a technical deep dive if you want one next week.
[09:23] Carlos: Yes, set up a deep dive — we may want an SE-only perf run.
[09:26] Samir: Will do. Thanks all.
[09:30] (meeting ends with some brief post-meeting small talk)
